CostAnomaly.description:
One anomaly entry surfaced on the dashboard.

Mirrors `CostAnomaly` in `services/admin/src/lib/types.ts`. Money is
integer cents to match the rest of the cost-api surface; the frontend
formats it for display. `signature` is the dedup key the alert-state
table uses (a stable hash of detector + tenant + dimension + window),
which lets the route mark a freshly-detected anomaly as `suppressed`
when the same signature is still inside its quiet-period window.

`first_seen` and `last_seen` are ISO-8601 UTC instants (matching the
`IsoTimestamp` type on the frontend). They differ when the same
signature has been re-observed before its quiet period expired; the
detector updates `last_seen` rather than emitting a fresh row.

detector.description: Detector name that emitted the anomaly.
detector.title: Detector

deviation_pct.description: Signed percent deviation from expected: (observed - expected) / expected * 100.
deviation_pct.title: Deviation Pct

dimension_key.description: Free-form dimension key the detector uses to label this anomaly.
dimension_key.title: Dimension Key

expected_cost_cents.description: Detector's expected cost for the same window in integer cents.
expected_cost_cents.title: Expected Cost Cents

first_seen.description: UTC instant the detector first saw this anomaly.
first_seen.title: First Seen

last_seen.description: UTC instant the detector most recently re-saw it.
last_seen.title: Last Seen

observed_cost_cents.description: Observed cost during the anomaly window in integer cents.
observed_cost_cents.title: Observed Cost Cents

signature.description: Stable dedup hash of the anomaly's dimensions.
signature.title: Signature

suppressed.description: True when the anomaly's dedup signature is in its active quiet period.
suppressed.title: Suppressed

tenant_id.description: Tenant the anomaly is attributed to, if any.
tenant_id.title: Tenant Id

CostAnomaly.title: CostAnomaly

CostForecast.description:
Full response envelope for `GET /api/v1/cost/forecast`.

Mirrors `CostForecast` in `services/admin/src/lib/types.ts`. The
forecast covers `horizon_days` consecutive days starting from
today (UTC). `model` identifies the forecasting backend so future
iterations can swap CE for a custom model without breaking the
contract; today the only value is `ce-builtin` (AWS Cost Explorer
`GetCostForecast`). `queried_at` is the wall-clock instant the
response was assembled, server-trusted so the dashboard can render
staleness without trusting the client's clock.

cache_hit.title: Cache Hit

horizon_days.title: Horizon Days

ForecastBucket.description:

`lower_bound_cents` and `upper_bound_cents` are the 95% prediction
interval bounds. All money is integer cents to match the rest of
the cost-api surface; the frontend formats it for display.

TenantCostRow.description:
One row of the per-tenant cost rollup.

Mirrors `TenantCostRow` in `services/admin/src/lib/types.ts`.
`display_name` defaults to the tenant id so the table renders cleanly
even before the user-directory join lands; future iterations will
populate it from the auth-db.

`services` is the per-service breakdown of the tenant's cost across
the window, sorted descending by `cost_cents`. Populated from the
rollup table's composite sort key (`day_service`, see ADR-040);
defaults to an empty tuple when the rollup is empty so older
snapshots without the dimension still deserialize cleanly.

cost_cents.title: Cost Cents

percent_of_total.description: Cost as a percent of the total spend in the window (0-100).
percent_of_total.title: Percent Of Total

services.description: Per-service breakdown of this tenant's cost, sorted desc by cost_cents.
services.title: Services

get.description:
Return the current cost-anomaly feed.

The dashboard's "Cost anomalies" page consumes this route. When
`active_only=true` (the default) the route reads the alert-state
table directly so the response is fast and CE-rate-limit-safe.

When `active_only=false` the route additionally fetches
detector-fresh anomalies from Cost Explorer for the last 30 days,
deduplicates against the active alert-state rows by `signature`,
and marks duplicates as `suppressed=true`. That lets operators see
the full detector picture (fresh + suppressed) when investigating
a paged anomaly's history.

The route returns an empty list (rather than a 5xx) when no Cost
Anomaly Monitor is configured upstream. The dashboard renders that
as a clean empty state with a hint to set one up. See the
follow-up section of `.agent-runs/<this-run>.md` for the Terraform
that creates the monitor.

parameters.description: Optional exact-match filter on the detector name.
parameters.name: detector

schema.description: Optional exact-match filter on the detector name.
schema.title: Detector

parameters.description: When true (default), return only the dedup-active alert-state rows. When false, also detect fresh anomalies from Cost Explorer for the last 30 days and mark each one as suppressed if its dedup signature matches an active alert-state row.
parameters.name: active_only

schema.description: When true (default), return only the dedup-active alert-state rows. When false, also detect fresh anomalies from Cost Explorer for the last 30 days and mark each one as suppressed if its dedup signature matches an active alert-state row.
schema.title: Active Only

parameters.description: Reserved for future shape variants; only 'list' is supported today.
parameters.name: kind

schema.description: Reserved for future shape variants; only 'list' is supported today.
schema.title: Kind

get.description:
Return AWS spend broken down by service for a date window.

Query parameters:
- `from`: inclusive start (ISO date).
- `to`:   exclusive end (ISO date).

The response includes a `cache_hit` flag the dashboard surfaces so
operators can tell at a glance whether the page was served from
DynamoDB or paid a CE round trip. `queried_at` is the wall-clock
instant the response was assembled (server-trusted).

Return AWS spend broken down by tenant for a date window.

Reads from `panakoes-dev-tenant-cost-rollup` (populated by the
nightly aggregator job, Phase 2.2). The route aggregates daily rows
into per-tenant totals across the window, sorts descending by cost,
and computes `percent_of_total` against the window's grand total
using integer-cents arithmetic.

The rollup table being empty (no aggregator run yet, or no activity
in the window) is a normal case: the response carries `tenants=()`
and `total_cents=0` rather than 404, matching the by-service
"zero-spend window" semantics the dashboard already handles.

Return CE's daily cost forecast for the next `horizon_days`.

Backed by `boto3 ce.GetCostForecast` (`Granularity=DAILY`,
`Metric=UNBLENDED_COST`, `PredictionIntervalLevel=95`). Each
response bucket carries the mean predicted spend plus the 95%
prediction-interval lower / upper bounds, all in integer cents.
The route does not cache the response: CE's forecast model
refreshes daily, the call is cheap, and the dashboard's horizon
dropdown re-fires the request on every change so a stale cache
would mostly hurt freshness with little CE-cost savings.

parameters.description: Number of consecutive days to forecast starting today (UTC). Must be one of 7, 14, 30, 60, 90.
parameters.name: horizon_days

schema.description: Number of consecutive days to forecast starting today (UTC). Must be one of 7, 14, 30, 60, 90.
schema.title: Horizon Days
